articles.title: "Life was going to end": Marshall Faulk’s NFL career was defined by speed and power; his Parkinson’s journey is now about something different
articles.summary: Marshall Faulk has Parkinson's disease, and he has known for about a year and a half. The Pro Football Hall of Famer, 53, shared the diagnosis with Dr.
articles.body: Marshall Faulk has Parkinson's disease, and he has known for about a year and a half. The Pro Football Hall of Famer, 53, shared the diagnosis with Dr. Sandeep Thakkar, host of The Caring Neurologist, on Wednesday, Oct. 21. Faulk, now head football coach at Southern University, says his symptoms have stayed mild so far, limited to hand rigidity and what he calls "little tremors." He wants other people to get checked early if something feels off.How Marshall Faulk found out about his Parkinson's diagnosisIt started on a golf course. Faulk felt rigidity in his hand while playing and figured the club might be to blame. Then it kept happening when he wasn't holding one.He brought it up with his doctor during a physical. The doctor didn't wait around and sent him to a specialist right away. Faulk says he is "anal" about his health, so he had no interest in putting it off."You tell me that and I'm going, like, I believe in going to the doctor," Faulk told Thakkar.Parkinson's is a neurodegenerative disorder that affects movement, according to the Parkinson's Foundation. Its cause is unknown, and there is no cure.Faulk doesn't see his diagnosis as terminal, and two people shaped that view. He met Muhammad Ali after Ali was diagnosed and came away struck by how "all there" the boxing great still was. He also pointed to Michael J. Fox, who has lived with Parkinson's since 1991."So, knowing that, I didn't look at it like if I got a diagnosis, life was going to end," Faulk said. "I treat it like -- I've had a bunch of surgeries on my right knee. There's some parts in it that aren't mine, that aren't original. My back, you know, it hurts every once in a while.""It's something you live with," Faulk continued. "It's not to where it's a detriment to your livelihood. Now, if you don't take care of it, there's an opportunity for that to be. But you have to take care of it."Why Marshall Faulk wants others to get checked earlyFaulk says he is speaking up for a simple reason. He hopes people who notice something odd in their own bodies will see a trained specialist instead of waiting."The earlier you catch it, the better chance you have at living a better quality of life with medication compared to if you catch it later, the things that you start to have, the things that you go through, it makes life a little bit more difficult," Faulk said.He feels he is in a solid spot right now. He hasn't yet had a full conversation with friends and family about the diagnosis. That will come, he said, "if it comes to a time where my lifestyle changes.""I'm functioning. I'm good. You know, I just think I caught it early," he said. "I'm in a good place."Faulk has plenty on his plate. He won a Super Bowl with the St. Louis Rams in 2000 and retired from the NFL in 2007. He entered the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2011, his first year of eligibility. Southern University hired him as head football coach in Baton Rouge, La., in December 2025, so he is dealing with the diagnosis while running a program.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2015, Aaron Rodgers bought a Wisconsin estate; 10 years later, his $3.7 million listing put it back in the spotlight
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers paid about $1.74 million for a custom stone house outside Green Bay in March 2015.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers paid about $1.74 million for a custom stone house outside Green Bay in March 2015. In November 2025, he listed it for $3.7 million, more than double. The roughly 10,500-square-foot home sits on 5.32 acres in Hobart, Wisconsin. He kept it through the end of his Packers career, two seasons with the Jets, and a fresh start with the Steelers. Daniel Posey of Coldwell Banker Real Estate Group holds the listing. The price is the headline. The timing says more.What Aaron Rodgers paid in 2015 and what he was asking laterAaron Rodgers was fresh off his second MVP award when he bought the place, and his Super Bowl win over Pittsburgh sat five years back. Pittsburgh is the team he plays for now, which gives the whole story an odd symmetry. The house dates to 2003 and had been listed on and off for years before he took it. His earlier Wisconsin purchase, a four-bedroom home in Suamico, cost just $442,500.The ask is now about $3.74 million, roughly 2.15 times his purchase price. That looks like a clean win, but it isn't pure profit. A decade of taxes, upkeep and agent fees chips away at the gain, and a house this big appeals to a small group of buyers.That small group is the real test. A Green Bay Press-Gazette roundup of former Packers homes described Kabeer Gbaja-Biamila's Hobart property, priced at $3.988 million, as having sat on the market for several years. Rodgers listed on November 10, 2025, and no sale had been reported at the time of writing.What does $3.7 million buy in Hobart?The house covers about 10,529 square feet on a cul-de-sac called Thayer Trail. It sits northwest of downtown Green Bay, and reports put it anywhere from a few miles to about 20 minutes from Lambeau Field. It has four bedrooms. Accounts disagree on bathrooms, with counts from 4.5 to seven, so check the listing itself if that detail matters.The main level has wide-plank hickory floors, a library, and a chef's kitchen with commercial-grade appliances, a walk-in pantry and a butler's pantry. Reports describe a lower level built for play, with a billiards room, arcade area, gym with a steam shower, wine room and a brick-walled theater.The layout favors crowds. It suits a player who hosts teammates and family and needs room to train, less so a couple after a quiet weekend place. Listing photos show the rooms cleared of Rodgers' belongings. That is standard staging, though it also makes the house feel finished with him.Why Aaron Rodgers kept pitching it to Packers playersRodgers never sat quietly on this property. In summer 2024, when Jordan Love signed a $220 million extension, Rodgers publicly suggested Love buy the house. Love didn't bite. He had plenty of reasons to wait. Rodgers finished 8-9 in his last Packers season, then went to New York in a trade that sent a first-, second- and sixth-round pick to Green Bay. He tore his Achilles four snaps into his Jets career. The house stayed put through all of it.In 2025 he tried again, this time with Micah Parsons, the defensive end Green Bay got from Dallas shortly before the season. The pitch came after Rodgers scrambled away from a Parsons sack in a game at Pittsburgh. Parsons told reporters, "And he told me to buy his house." Parsons said he had looked at it but didn't need something so large, and he pointed to tight end Tucker Kraft as a possible taker. ESPN noted the house hadn't appeared in any public listing at that point.Here is my read. A quarterback making sales calls to Packers players isn't chasing the top dollar. He wanted a buyer who would understand the place, and the locker room is one of the few groups nearby that can afford it. When that route stalled, a public listing was what remained.Where Aaron Rodgers' other homes standWisconsin is one of three homes on the market. A Realtor.com report put the combined asking price at $58.2 million. Malibu leads at $39.5 million, a beachfront property he bought for $28 million in 2019. At full price, that would be an $11.5 million gain, about 41%, over seven years. His New Jersey house, bought through an LLC in 2023 for $9.5 million, is listed at $15 million.Rodgers and his wife, Brittani, now live in Canonsburg, Pennsylvania, outside Pittsburgh. Reports describe an equestrian estate there with stables, a six-car garage and a par-3 golf course. He signed a one-year deal with the Steelers and has made clear this is his final NFL season.Of the three listings, Wisconsin is the smallest sale and the oldest tie. It is also the only one he tried to sell face to face.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Kenneth Walker III has found new heights in Kansas City, while Seattle’s run game tells a different story
articles.summary: Kenneth Walker III faces the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday night, and few running backs have arrived at a reunion in better form.
articles.body: Kenneth Walker III faces the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday night, and few running backs have arrived at a reunion in better form. He left as the Super Bowl LX MVP after rushing for 135 yards, then signed a three-year, $45 million deal with Kansas City. Through five games, he leads the league with 665 rushing yards and a 6.3 average. He has also scored six rushing touchdowns. Seattle ranks 31st in EPA per rush. According to The Athletic, the Seahawks never offered him an extension before free agency. That choice looks costly now.Kenneth Walker has lifted a Chiefs run game that lacked punchThe numbers are hard to argue with. Walker also leads in rushing yards over expected with 277, or 2.7 per attempt, and in broken tackles with 52. He sits second in rushing touchdowns and in runs of 10 or more yards, with 19. He is one of only six players since 1950 to reach 750 scrimmage yards and eight touchdowns through five games. The others are Jim Brown, Eric Dickerson, Emmitt Smith, Marshall Faulk and Priest Holmes.Kansas City has not had a 1,000-yard rusher in the Patrick Mahomes era. That drought will not last long. Walker has already passed the 611 yards Kareem Hunt led the team with all of last season.He is also getting the ball more than ever. Walker has 106 carries, or 21.2 per game, which puts him on pace for about 360. He never carried 228 times in a season with the Seahawks. Seattle split the work with Zach Charbonnet after drafting him in 2023. In Kansas City, the backfield is his alone.The run game has changed how the whole offense looks. Last season the Chiefs ran 196 plays from under center, 40 of them passes. They already have 121 through five games, again with 40 passes. Play-action throws are at 57, compared with 150 all of last year, and Kansas City ranks sixth in EPA per pass at 0.27, per Next Gen Stats. It was 16th at 0.05. Being ahead has helped. The Chiefs have trailed only against the Colts in Week 2 and the Raiders in Week 4, and never by more than seven, so they never had to abandon the run.Seattle's ground game has slipped since he leftSeattle has the opposite problem. The Seahawks rank 31st in EPA per rush at minus 0.24, while Walker leads the league at 0.12 per attempt. Injuries explain a lot. Charbonnet is working back from a torn ACL suffered in the divisional round, and first-round pick Jadarian Price is on injured reserve. Price had 119 yards at 4.3 a carry before his Week 3 injury, fumbles aside. Without both, Sam Darnold has had little help from the ground.Sunday still won't be easy for Walker.Seattle allows 96 rushing yards a game, tenth in the league, and has yet to give up 70 to any back. Walker has topped 96 in four of five games. Only Miami held him under 100, and the Dolphins are tied with Seattle for fourth in EPA per rush allowed. The Seahawks will need to copy that plan.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Peyton Manning was recently linked as a potential general manager for the Indianapolis Colts organization after billionaire owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon gave up on decade-long GM Chris Ballard midseason.The connection felt uncanny because Manning is remembered as one of the greatest quarterbacks in the Indianapolis Colts’ history. He gifted them a Super Bowl after 36 years.However, he spent the final four seasons of his NFL career with the Denver Broncos. Manning also gifted the Broncos a Super Bowl after 17 years. He has since settled in Denver, Colorado.The NFL Hall of Famer’s mansion in Cherry Hills Village is best known for its expansive interiors, traditional architecture, and luxurious amenities.The ManningCast host purchased it for nearly $5 million in 2012. The opulent abode covers approximately 17,000 sq. ft. across 3.37 acres, making it one of the most stunning celebrity homes in the Denver Area.Peyton Manning’s Cherry Hills Village mansion detailsPeyton Manning’s massive mansion lies in the affluent suburb of Cherry Hills Village near Denver. The luxurious estate became the NFL legend’s home after he signed with the Denver Broncos in 2012.According to Omni Home Ideas, the massive property was built in 2004. It features seven bedrooms and ten bathrooms. The 16,464 sq. ft. residence was purchased for $4.57 million, but its estimated value is approximately $6.01 million, as of November 2024.The securely gated estate boasts immense privacy and significant outdoor space. The location keeps the two-time Super Bowl champion connected to the Colorado community where he built his base after bidding goodbye to Indianapolis.Peyton Manning home’s exteriors and interiorsThe Georgian-style estate exudes timeless elegance and Peyton Manning’s iconic legacy with its red-brick exterior, white architectural accents, symmetrical windows, and prominent entrance columns. Elegant columns support the second-floor balcony.The interiors perfectly balance classic, comfortable design with modern, royal luxury. A grand hallway features white crown molding and soft beige walls, along with a sweeping wrought-iron staircase that draws attention without overdoing the space.The living room features massive windows, warm-toned furnishings, and a traditional fireplace. Plush armchairs and sofas surround a classic white fireplace mantel. Elegant golden drapery frames the massive windows, flooding the room with natural light.A mahogany-paneled study boasts built-in shelves for books and memorabilia, thereby creating a warm and sophisticated workplace for the former NFL quarterback.The mansion also features a dedicated game room with a rich wooden pool table, where its green-felt surface glows in the natural light coming in through the massive windows.The multi-million-dollar mansion’s gourmet kitchen features white cabinetry, black granite countertops, and a central island perfect for food preparation and casual dining. Elegant barstools with wrought-iron frames surround the island, thereby enhancing its utility.Wrought-iron lighting fixtures provide practical and decorative appeal, complementing the hardwood floors below. An additional dining area offers space for hosting guests.The main bedroom suite’s best feature is its French doors, which open to a private balcony and invite ample sunlight and fresh air. The bedroom suite has understated beige interiors and decorative ceiling moldings, thereby adding a refined touch to the inner space.The spa-like bathroom features marble finishes, a glass-enclosed walk-in shower, double vanities with ornate cabinetry, and polished brass fixtures, exuding pure sophistication.The walk-in closet features custom-built shelves and hanging spaces in deep wood tones, thereby offering an organized and aesthetically pleasing storage solution.Peyton Manning’s Cherry Hills home’s outdoor spaceThe outdoor space of Peyton Manning’s Cherry Hills home boasts a covered patio which is framed by brick columns.It offers a private spot for alfresco dining. The wrought-iron furniture adds an old-world elegance to its Georgian style. The outdoor space also features a built-in outdoor kitchen with a high-end grill and a dedicated preparation area.The massive property is surrounded by lush greenery, while seasonal flowers add vibrant reds and yellows to the aesthetic landscape.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Jonathan Taylor, Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner and Top Landing Spots
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts are not yet ready to enter sell mode prior to the Nov. 10 trade deadline, though that could change depending on how they play over the next three games leading up to the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are not yet ready to enter sell mode prior to the Nov. 10 trade deadline, though that could change depending on how they play over the next three games leading up to the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

Per The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , the Colts want "to see what the landscape is like in a few weeks" before making any decision about engaging teams in trade talks for Jonathan Taylor.

NFL insider Tom Pelissero added DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson have generated "strong trade interest" and no one on the Colts roster, including Taylor, is "expected to be off limits" if they decide to be a seller prior to the trade deadline.

Jones cited the Minnesota Vikings and New York Giants as two potential suitors for Taylor if he becomes available.

Buckner and Nelson would seem more likely to be traded than Taylor because they are both in the final year of their current contracts.

Taylor just signed a two-year, $44 million extension in August that keeps him under contract through the 2028 season.

Buckner made it clear he's not happy where things are at with the Colts right now after their 26-20 loss to the Tennessee Titans in Week 6.

One popular landing spot for Buckner if he gets traded is a reunion with the San Francisco 49ers, who traded him to Indianapolis after the 2019 season. Niners fullback Kyle Juszczyk is in favor of bringing him back based on a social media post.

A team like the Green Bay Packers, who signed Laken Tomlinson, Mekhi Becton and Kevin Zeitler in the span of three days after Week 3 because their protection was so bad, could be a landing spot for Nelson if they want to add more help.

Taylor would almost certainly bring back the biggest return of this trio, but it would leave an already-thin group of skill-position players in Indianapolis bereft of talent.

Aaron Jones has been solid as the starting running back for Minnesota, but Taylor would represent a significant upgrade for a 5-0 team with Super Bowl aspirations.

The Giants running backs are a mess right now. Cam Skattebo leads the team with 294 rushing yards, but he didn't get a carry in just six offensive snaps in Week 6 against the New Orleans Saints.

Najee Harris, who was second on the Giants with 31 carries, got released on Tuesday.

Times are tough right now for a Colts team that will send its 2027 first-round pick to the New York Jets in the final piece to pay off the Sauce Gardner trade from November 2025.

The Colts have already made one significant move by firing longtime general manager Chris Ballard on Monday following a 26-20 loss to the Tennessee Titans in Week 6.

Ed Dodds, who has worked in Indianapolis' front office since 2017, was named interim general manager.

The Colts are in a difficult spot right now because of deals Ballard made over the past 12 months. In addition to the Gardner trade, he gave Daniel Jones an $88 million contract and Alec Pierce a four-year, $116 million deal in free agency.

Jones has thrown six interceptions to four touchdowns this season. Pierce has played in just two games due to heel issues stemming from offseason ankle surgery.

articles.title: NFL commissioner Roger Goodell on potential Tokyo game: 'It's coming at some point in the near future'
articles.summary: The NFL previously hosted 14 preseason games in Japan from 1976 to 2005.
articles.body:
The NFL has its eyes on returning to Japan with a game potentially happening in 2027 or 2028, according to commissioner Roger Goodell.

Appearing on the "NFL Daily" podcast this week , Goodell said the league's goal is to hold a regular-season game in Tokyo at some point over the next two seasons.

"Listen, Tokyo is clearly on our list, whether it's next year or the year after," Goodell said. "It's coming at some point in the near future."

It's not a matter of if, but when at this point. Goodell's comments come nearly two months after NFL executive vice president of club business and international and league events Peter O'Reilly said the league had been researching returning to Japan for a game and three months since Goodell named the country as one that was being targeted as a host city.

A regular-season NFL game has never been played in Japan, but the league did host 14 preseason games there between 1976 to 2005 — 13 in Tokyo and one in Osaka.

The success of the San Francisco 49ers-Los Angeles Rams Week 1 game in Melbourne, Australia, has played a role in helping the NFL learn how to pull off such a game.

"On a Friday morning at 10:30, to have 100,000 people in the stadium, it was just an incredible feeling for us. I think it's opened up new opportunities for us," Goodell said. "The travel is something we think we can manage and do it without impacting negatively on the teams. So each of these we learned something from and we benefit and we also open those other doors."

Should the NFL go to Japan, the Los Angeles Rams would likely be one of the teams involved. Under the league's Global Markets Program , the team has marketing rights in the country.

The NFL would like to increase the number of international games per season to 16 in the future. For now, owners approved a proposal to play up to 10 outside of the U.S. in 2027. Currently, there are five international games scheduled next season with Berlin, Mexico City and London (three games) set to host.

The New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers will play the sixth international game on the 2026 schedule this Sunday from Stade de France in Paris . Three more international games will be left to be played this season in Madrid, Munich and Mexico City.

articles.title: Cowboys' 'Perfect' Trade Target Revealed by NFL Execs in New Rumors Ahead of 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: As the Dallas Cowboys continue to try to reshape their defense, a high-profile pass-rusher has emerged as a potential trade target.
articles.body:
As the Dallas Cowboys continue to try to reshape their defense, a high-profile pass-rusher has emerged as a potential trade target.

During an appearance Saturday on SportsCenter , ESPN NFL insider Jeremy Fowler reported that anonymous league executives believe Arizona Cardinals pass-rusher Josh Sweat would be the "perfect profile fit" for Dallas.

"The problem with the Cowboys is they don't have a lot of draft picks but they're looking always for help, and there are pass-rushers," Fowler said. "I'll start with Josh Sweat in Arizona. I checked with a few league execs with other teams who believe that Dallas and Josh Sweat would be a perfect profile fit. Arizona, sitting at 2-4, could try to acquire more draft capital. Edge rusher is a position to watch over the next few weeks leading up to that Nov. 10 deadline. We will see if Sweat is involved in that, there's been some trade rumors around him for a while."

Insiders Name Sleeper Trade Candidates 💤

There is little doubt that the Cowboys need to do something in order to improve on the defensive side of the ball, as they rank 30th in total defense, 25th in scoring defense and tied for 27th in sacks.

Dallas acquired defensive tackle Quinnen Williams in a trade with the New York Jets last season and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers already this season, but neither move has helped the Cowboys move up the ranks defensively.

However, getting a player who can consistently pressure and sack the quarterback could potentially change things since the Cowboys have been missing that element since trading Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers prior to the 2025 season.

Sweat, 29, is in the midst of his second season with the Cards after signing a four-year, $76.4 million deal in free agency in 2025.

He spent his first seven seasons with the Philadelphia Eagles, earning one Pro Bowl selection and a Super Bowl win during that time.

Sweat had 43 sacks in 104 regular-season games for the Eagles, but he was at his best on the big stage, recording five sacks in nine playoff games, including 2.5 in Philly's Super Bowl LIX win over the Kansas City Chiefs.

In his first campaign as a member of the Cardinals in 2025, Sweat set a new career high with 12 sacks to go along with four forced fumbles, 30 tackles, 13 tackles for loss and 17 quarterback hits.

Through six games this season, Sweat has registered two sacks, 14 tackles, three tackles for loss and four quarterback hits.

Although the Cardinals are coming off a huge upset win over the Los Angeles Rams, they are still just 2-4 on the season and not expected to vie for a playoff spot.

Because of that, Sweat could possibly become a trade chip as the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaches.

Should that be the case, he figures to generate a ton of interest from contenders thanks to his history of playoff success, so it is fair to wonder if the Cowboys would have the assets to get a deal done after trading multiple picks for Williams and Porter already.

articles.title: Saints vs. Steelers in Paris: What the NFL House closure means amid protests across the city
articles.summary: NFL House in Paris has closed, one day after the league shut its pop-up shop, as France prepares for another round of nationwide protests.
articles.body: NFL House in Paris has closed, one day after the league shut its pop-up shop, as France prepares for another round of nationwide protests. The league cited possible accessibility issues. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said up to 70,000 officers will be deployed Saturday. The Steelers have already canceled their fan event in Bastille, and the Saints moved theirs to Sunday. Still, the league says Sunday’s game at Stade de France will go ahead. It will be the NFL’s first regular-season game in France. The Steelers are 4-2, the Saints 2-4.What the NFL House closure means for fans in ParisFor fans who flew in, the closures remove the easiest places to meet up. No reopening date has been reported. The Saints postponed their own gathering too, announcing that “Saints House has been postponed until Sunday.”The timing is awkward for the league. On Oct. 18, it said, “There’s been no disruption or impact at league sites.” On Thursday, the Steelers canceled Steelers House, a bar event in Bastille. “Following recent events in the Bastille neighborhood, and after careful consideration, we felt it appropriate not to move forward with the planned Steelers House fan event in Paris,” the team told fans. Nicki Ewell, the NFL’s vice president for global events, said that day no league fan events had been affected. By Saturday, the league’s own pop-up shop and NFL House were closed too.Dani Watt, wife of Steelers linebacker T.J. Watt, questioned the decision to play in Paris.Protests and security around Sunday’s NFL gamePolice approved one march on Saturday, from Bastille to Nation, and banned every other demonstration in Paris. Authorities closed 24 metro stations, the Louvre and the Orsay Museum. The U.S. State Department urged “Americans in Paris for the NFL game” to “exercise caution and be aware of their surroundings.”The unrest began in mid-September, when high school students protested overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages and outdated facilities. Trade unions and the yellow vests movement joined over the rising cost of living. Demonstrations on Oct. 17 drew more than 500,000 people nationwide, and police arrested more than 2,000 in Paris.Commissioner Roger Goodell said Wednesday, “We’ve made all the preparations.” He added, “Protests are not unusual in France, as you know, and that’s something that we will be aware of and make sure that the appropriate arrangements are made.” Peter O’Reilly, the league’s executive vice president for club business, said canceling or moving the game was never seriously considered. On Friday, French President Emmanuel Macron hosted Goodell, Saints owner Gayle Benson and Steelers president Art Rooney II at the Élysée Palace to discuss the game and the NFL’s long-term future in Paris.The guest list says plenty. The league is protecting a bigger bet on France than one Sunday. Kickoff is at Stade de France, in Saint-Denis, on the outskirts of the city.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Disappointed You’d Do This,’ ‘Mind Your Own Business’ — Fans Criticize Ex-NFL QB’s Assessment of Patrick Mahomes’ Role in Kenneth Walker III’s Success
articles.summary: Kenneth Walker III is the NFL’s leading rusher for a Kansas City Chiefs team that is 5-0 heading into Sunday night. That’s when he returns to Lumen Field to...
articles.body:
Kenneth Walker III is the NFL's leading rusher for a Kansas City Chiefs team that is 5-0 heading into Sunday night. That's when he returns to Lumen Field to face the Seattle Seahawks for the first time since leaving in free agency. He helped Seattle win Super Bowl LX last season.

But this week, the conversation around his success turned to Patrick Mahomes' left hand. ESPN analyst and former NFL quarterback Dan Orlovsky broke down what he read as hand signals from the quarterback to Walker in the run game. Two days before kickoff, fans responded with sharp criticism.

Dan Orlovsky's Breakdown of Patrick Mahomes' Hand Signals Draws Fire

Orlovsky posted a clip from ESPN's "NFL Live" that breaks down the Chiefs' running plays.

He pointed to Mahomes' left hand before the snap. On one play against a four-man front, Mahomes balled his hand into a fist, and on another against a five-man front he appeared to raise a single finger.

"I think those hand signals are a way where Patrick is communicating to Kenneth Walker, 'This is what the run game blocking is, code-wise or call side,' and it's giving him an advantage of what to expect when it comes to those blocks," Orlovsky said.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

The breakdown landed while the Chiefs prepared for their trip to Seattle, and some of the replies took aim at his motives. One fan wrote, "Dan out here doing everything he can to try and hurt the Chiefs in order to help his babydoll, Josh Allen."

Another fan also brought the Buffalo Bills quarterback into it: "This is what Dan 'Josh Allen is the greatest QB' Orlovsky will do, snitch. Dan, what is Allen saying to cook?"

Earlier in the week, on Monday, Oct. 19, Orlovsky spoke on "The Pat McAfee Show." He is an MVP voter, and he said, "If MVP voting was happening today, I would vote for Kenneth Walker."

Snitching Complaints Meet a Caveat From Orlovsky's Own Clip

Other replies focused on what the clip might give away. One fan asked, "Do other QB too! Why only snitching on Mahomes"

Another fan predicted that the "Chiefs will have to come up with something else new now."

Orlovsky had addressed that concern in the same clip: "And just for Chiefs fans, this isn't something that's going to make you predictable, or teams are going to be able to steal it."

The criticism may be somewhat overblown. Orlovsky was analyzing tendencies visible on game film, the same kind of material opposing coaches and scouting staffs study each week, and he did not reveal any confirmed Chiefs terminology or proprietary play-call information.

That makes the backlash notable more for how strongly fans reacted to the segment than for any evidence that Orlovsky actually gave Kansas City's opponents something they did not already have access to.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Others aimed their frustration at Orlovsky personally. "With you being a former QB, I'm disappointed you'd do this," one fan wrote.

Another wrote, "Dan is the worst. Mind your own business."

Another fan came at the segment from a different direction: "If that's true…why is it ESPN worthy? A QB leading his team. Seems pretty routine."

Attention on the Chiefs' ground game follows their move on Walker this offseason. They signed the 26-year-old to a three-year, $43 million contract after his 135-yard MVP performance in the Seahawks' Super Bowl win over the New England Patriots.

Through five games, he has 665 rushing yards on 106 carries, and his 6.3 yards per carry ranks first among 43 qualified rushers. According to Next Gen Stats, his 277 rush yards over expected also rank first among 40 qualified rushers. Pro Football Network's NFL RB Impact Grade has Walker at 96.5 so far this season, making him the top-ranked running back of 45 graded.

His latest game was the Chiefs' 22-6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers on Oct. 18, when he ran for 128 yards and two touchdowns on 19 carries.

PFN posted "the top offensive players from NFL Week 6, per PFN's Impact metrics." Walker was the running back on the list, and three of the linemen who block for him, guards Trey Smith and Kingsley Suamataia and center Creed Humphrey, made it too.

Kickoff on "Sunday Night Football" is set for 8:20 p.m. ET. The Chiefs, first in the AFC West, will face a Seahawks defense that has not allowed a running back to reach 100 yards since Week 8 of the 2024 season.

articles.title: How Brendan Sorsby is preparing for 2027 NFL Draft after being banned from college football
articles.summary: Former NCAA football player Brendan Sorsby is preparing to compete for a spot in the NFL. Sorsby was essentially banned from playing in college football duri...

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy 'Impressed from the Moment He' Joined Giants After Vikings Trade, NFL Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy reportedly started turning his image around immediately after he was traded from the Minnesota Vikings.
articles.body:
New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy reportedly started turning his image around immediately after he was traded from the Minnesota Vikings.

NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday McCarthy "has impressed from the moment he entered the building in New York with his attitude and approach."

"A primary focus this week has been on a clean operation—making sure McCarthy can call plays he largely has never run before and get in and out of the huddle efficiently," Pelissero reported.

Coach John Harbaugh announced Wednesday McCarthy would be making the first start of his Giants career in Sunday's Week 7 action against the Houston Texans.

McCarthy played his first significant action for the Giants in relief of Jameis Winston against the New Orleans Saints in Week 6, when he helped chip away at a 24-point deficit to get his team within one score of tying the game.

He finished the fourth quarter having gone 11-for-21 with 243 passing yards, a touchdown and an interception while gaining 26 yards on two carries.

The Athletic's Dan Duggan reported Thursday McCarthy's ability to fill in for Jaxson Dart's absence from the Giants' run game played a role in Harbaugh's decision to name him the team's Week 7 starter.

"It was immediately evident that the coaching staff viewed McCarthy's legs as an asset," Duggan reported. "Even as he was cramming to learn the playbook, the coaches installed quarterback-run packages for McCarthy."

McCarthy is about to test out those packages against one of the most effective run defenses in the league. The Texans have allowed the third-fewest rushing yards against in the NFL during the team's 2-4 start to the season.

The Giants and Texans are set to kick off the Week 7 matchup at 1 p.m. ET in Houston.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson's Contract Addressed by Jimmy Haslam as Browns Lead AFC North in NFL Standings
articles.summary: As one of the surprise stories of the NFL season thus far, the Cleveland Browns aren't ready to make any declarations about Deshaun Watson's future with the organization.
articles.body:
As one of the surprise stories of the NFL season thus far, the Cleveland Browns aren't ready to make any declarations about Deshaun Watson's future with the organization.

Browns owner Jimmy Haslam told The Athletic's Jonathan Jones it would be "way premature" to discuss Watson's contract.

"That's way premature to talk about that," Haslam said. "We're just focused on beating the (Tennessee) Titans."

Even though Haslam doesn't want to tip his hand at this point, Jones quoted one NFL source who thinks the "door is wide open" for Watson to remain in Cleveland beyond 2026.

"The door is wide open for him to be with the Browns," the NFL source said. "It's the only line on a starting quarterback job he'll have. And even if you are in position to take one high, or get in position to do so, you're in no rush to play the rookie."

Cleveland is an interesting spot right now with a 4-2 record through six games. There's a tremendous amount of young talent on the roster, including Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion, Harold Fannin Jr., Carson Schwesinger and Mason Graham.

The Browns also own two first-round picks in the 2027 draft thanks to the Myles Garrett trade with the Los Angeles Rams. Based on the current draft order , the Rams' pick would be at No. 11 overall.

Despite their strong start, Watson's play still leaves something to be desired. He has been sacked an NFL-high 24 times, is tied for the league lead with six fumbles and ranks 25th out of 33 quarterbacks in QBR. He is 16th out of 21 quarterbacks in EPA per play and 17th out of 21 quarterbacks in success rate (min. 200 plays).

Cleveland has scored more than 21 points once in six games. The Browns have been good in close and late-game situations, with Watson tied for the league lead in game-winning drives at four.

This season marks the final year of Watson's five-year, $230 million contract signed in March 2022 after he was acquired in a trade with the Houston Texans, though he will still count against their cap through 2030 due to void years.

Another argument for the Browns to potentially keep Watson on a new contract is he is set to count $86.2 million in dead money on their 2027 cap, though they can spread that out over two seasons by designating him as a post-June 1 cut before March 13, 2027.

If the Browns could potentially find a way to lower that number, even if they are able to draft a quarterback early in the 2027 draft, it might be financially beneficial to their cap to keep Watson around.

For now, though, the Browns can focus their attention on trying to remain in the mix in a very competitive AFC North. All four teams enter Week 7 with winning records.

Cleveland, by virtue of having wins over the Pittsburgh Steelers and Baltimore Ravens, is officially in first place going into Sunday. This is the first time since 2014 season the Browns have led the division outright at any point in the season.

articles.title: Latest on Brendan Sorsby's Prep for 2027 NFL Draft Revealed in New Rumors
articles.summary: Quarterback Brendan Sorsby is working with a former NFL coach to prepare for the 2027 draft, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday on his Substack.
articles.body:
Quarterback Brendan Sorsby is working with a former NFL coach to prepare for the 2027 draft, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday on his Substack.

"Sorsby could emerge as one of the 2027 draft's top QB prospects... While he's not playing football this fall, Sorsby is getting plenty of work on the practice field," Pelissero reported.

According to Pelissero, Sorsby is spending the season working with former NFL quarterbacks coach Rich Scangarello.

Scangarello worked for seven NFL teams from 2009 to 2024, including a stint as offensive coordinator for the 2019 Denver Broncos.

His tenure in the league included stints overlapping with Kyle Shanahan on the Atlanta Falcons and San Francisco 49ers coaching staffs, Pelissero noted.

According to Pelissero, Scangarello is using that experience to teach Sorsby what language the 49ers' offense would use against NFL defenses.

"Each week, Scangarello installs two to three more 49ers offensive plays to beat specific looks each defensive play caller presents," Pelissero reported. "Then, Sorsby drills each aspect of the game plan—third down, protections, red zone, etc.—in three weekly throwing sessions tied to what he's learning."

Sorsby spent two seasons with Indiana before transferring to Cincinnati ahead of the 2024 season. Over two seasons with the Bearcats, he completed 62.9 percent of his passes for 5,613 yards with 45 touchdowns and 12 interceptions.

The NFL ruled in June Sorsby would be eligible to participate in pre-draft activities including the Senior Bowl, pro day and team visits before entering the 2027 draft. Sorsby will hope his training sets him up for success during that span despite not having taken a game rep since November 2025.

articles.title: El caso de la superestrella que está a punto de igualar el récord de más derrotas de la NFL
articles.standfirst: Matthew Stafford puede empatar esta semana el peor registro de un quarterback en la liga. Este ranking, sin embargo, sólo está integrado por grandes QB
articles.summary: Matthew Stafford puede empatar esta semana el peor registro de un quarterback en la liga. Este ranking, sin embargo, sólo está integrado por grandes QB
articles.body: Esta semana los Los Angeles Rams (2-4) se enfrentan a Las Vegas Riders (3-3). Los angelinos arrancaron la temporada como uno de los favoritos para ganar la Super Bowl, pero tras seis semanas, es un equipo que da la sensación de que tendrá problemas para estar en los playoffs. Para su quarterback Matthew Stafford, una derrota adelantará algo que está destinado a suceder esta temporada. Sería la derrota número 123 de su carrera, dato que lo igualaría a Vinny Testaverde como el QB con un mayor número de partidos perdidos en la historia de la NFL. Sin duda, un récord negativo que a nadie le gustaría poseer, pero que a su vez habla de una longeva carrera en la liga. Para estar entre los primeros de este ranking hay que jugar durante muchos años y, en general, hacerlo bien para mantenerse como titular. En el caso de Stafford, tiene ahora 38 años y ha estado en la NFL desde 2009, cuando los Detroit Lions lo seleccionaron como número 1 del Draft. Durante sus 12 temporadas en Detroit, ganó muchos partidos, pero no pudo llevar a su franquicia lejos, y es que nunca ganó un partido de playoffs (disputó tres). Finalmente solicitó ser traspasado y acabó en los Rams en 2021. Durante su primera temporada en Los Ángeles, Stafford no sólo ganó el primer partido de playoffs de su carrera, sino que también lideró a los Rams a la victoria en el Super Bowl LVI, por lo que su estatus de gran estrella quedó de algún modo legitimado. En 2025 fue elegido MVP por primera vez en su trayectoria en la liga y con tales logros en su palmarés parece que quedó consagrado para acceder al Salón de la Fama en el futuro. Por desgracia, es cuestión de tiempo que lidere la lista de derrotas de los QB, pues todavía queda mucha temporada.

articles.title: Troy Aikman Says He’d Consider Role With the Cowboys
articles.summary: Aikman welcomes conversations with Jerry Jones as his ESPN contract nears expiration.
articles.body:
Troy Aikman says he realizes that his broadcasting career "could very well be taken away from me," and he'd consider a role with the Cowboys if owner Jerry Jones were interested in that.

Aikman's comments to Mike Fisher of Cowboys Roundtable came after recent reports by Front Office Sports that there is tension between Aikman and his Monday Night Football broadcasting partner, Joe Buck, and that Aikman has no formal and ongoing agreement to serve as a consultant with the Dolphins.

Speculation about Aikman's future has been rampant since FOS reported that he and Buck had an argument before a recent Rams-Bills game.

Jones said Wednesday at the conclusion of the NFL owners meeting in New York, in response to a question by FOS , that he's following Aikman's situation with ESPN and that Aikman would be capable of serving in a front office role for an NFL franchise if he so desires.

"This week he said some really kind things, which meant a lot to me, quite honestly," Aikman told Fisher. "So, yeah, I would welcome any conversation with Jerry. And quite honestly I don't know if there would be or if there ever would be an opportunity. But if Jerry came to me and felt that, in his heart, I could lend some services that would help make them better, I would. I'd have a hard time not taking a good look at that."

Aikman served as a consultant to the Dolphins last offseason, but his formal consulting agreement with Miami was limited to the team's general manager and head coach searches, FOS reported.

Jones said Wednesday that he pays "a lot of attention" to Aikman, adding: "And he's very capable of doing any one of a number of things, certainly anything to do with football. I don't know of any area, short of getting back out on the field … that Troy Aikman wouldn't be qualified and competent to go into."

Aikman, 59, is a Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback who played for Jones and the Cowboys for 12 seasons, leading them to three Super Bowl titles. He has been critical at times in recent years of Jones's ownership approach with the Cowboys.

Fisher asked Aikman whether he would be willing to go to lunch with Jones.

"I absolutely would," Aikman said. "I would have lunch, breakfast, or dinner with Jerry any time he wants it. And it wouldn't necessarily have to be because it's a job interview. Just because, you know, we go back a long way. … When I came in, I was 22 years old. I was his very first draft pick. There's a lot within that relationship, both from the beginning when he began as the owner, when I began my NFL career as a quarterback for 12 years of my life playing for him.

"And then even in the years that have followed, you know, we've been through a lot. We've been through the highest of highs. We've been through some pretty tough moments as well. Our relationship is complicated. I think he would agree with that. But it is one that's built, I believe, on respect."

Aikman's contract with ESPN expires after the network's Super Bowl broadcast.

Hans Schroeder, the NFL's EVP and chief media officer, said Wednesday in New York that the league had "no concern" about Aikman's issues with Buck and ESPN.

"And now as I'm into my last year at ESPN, I'm realizing that this is something that could very well be taken away from me," Aikman told Fisher. "And so for the first time, I'm realizing how much I really do—I've always enjoyed it. I've always known that. But until you risk having something taken away from you, I think sometimes you tend to maybe take things for granted.

"And so for the first time probably in my career, I'm realizing, you know, this is a great profession. It's been a great ride for me. And I hope that it's not over. Time will tell. But, yeah, so we'll see. I'm excited about what the rest of this year holds. And I'm excited to finally get back into the booth for a Super Bowl. … And now it will have been eight years since we last called a Super Bowl."

articles.title: Lamar Jackson Out for Ravens vs. Bengals, Latest Updates on QB's Ankle Injury

"Right now, I'm headed in the right direction," Jackson told reporters Friday. "I can't call it right now, still got a grace period. We'll see, man, hopefully. But I feel like I'm heading in the right direction right now."

He initially suffered the ankle sprain during Baltimore's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 4.

The Ravens have turned to backup quarterback Tyler Huntley in Jackson's absence, and will do so again Sunday.

Huntley led the Ravens to a 30-23 overtime win against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5 before falling to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6.

articles.title: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks Out for Eagles vs. Cowboys, Latest on WR's Injuries
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles will be without wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks when they host the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night due to hamstring and ankle injuries, respectively.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles will be without wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks when they host the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night due to hamstring and ankle injuries, respectively.

Philadelphia has a lengthy injury report as they look to snap a four-game losing streak. Beyond Smith and Wicks, running back Saquon Barkley is questionable to play as he continues to recover from a hamstring injury. Tight end Dallas Goedert has no game designation after logging a full practice on Saturday.

The Eagles have been hit hard this year, to say the least, particularly on the offensive side of the ball.

Quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss the rest of the season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in his lungs. Right tackle Lane Johnson has retired . Guard Landon Dickerson has been out with a knee injury since Week 1 and suffered a pectoral injury Thursday during practice, but he may return Monday.

Barkley and Goedert have missed two games, and Smith will now sit his third.

All told, the season has been a nightmare. Philadelphia is 28th in points per game (17.7 PPG), and there doesn't seem to be a clear answer in sight given how shorthanded the team will be.

The silver lining is that the Eagles play in a weak NFC East and sit tied for second with the 2-4 Cowboys. The 3-2-1 New York Giants pace the division, but they've endured numerous season-ending injuries (Jaxson Dart, edge-rusher Brian Burns, linebacker Tremaine Edmunds) and may not run away with the division.

For now, the Eagles will forge ahead and hope to break their slide. Darius Cooper, who has caught half of his eight receptions for touchdowns, figures to be the interim WR1. Rookie Makai Lemon should also see his fair share of looks.

Kickoff in Philadelphia on Monday is set for 8:15 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Josh Allen, after raising $140,230 for children's hospital, brings back $49.99 charity caps
articles.summary: Josh Allen is turning his NFL game-day tradition into another opportunity to give back.
articles.body: Josh Allen is turning his NFL game-day tradition into another opportunity to give back. The Buffalo Bills quarterback has teamed up with New Era for a new edition of the Billustration cap collection, with proceeds benefiting the Patricia Allen Fund at Golisano Children's Hospital of Buffalo.Announced on August 31, 2026, the latest collection features eight caps designed by children receiving care at the hospital. Each cap is listed at $49.99, giving fans a way to support the cause while adding a piece of Allen's charitable initiative to their collection.Josh Allen's $49.99 charity caps return with $17 million fundraising milestoneThe campaign builds on an impressive result from the previous season. In 2025, auctions of custom hats worn by Allen during Bills home games raised $140,230 for the Patricia Allen Fund. The signed caps, featuring artwork inspired by young hospital patients, turned Allen's game-day appearances into a fundraising opportunity.However, the new collection's fundraising total has not yet been publicly confirmed. New Era has not disclosed a fixed donation amount per cap or a percentage of sales that will go to the fund, so the $49.99 retail price should not be confused with the amount donated.The latest cap campaign is part of a much larger philanthropic effort. In June 2026, the Patricia Allen Fund surpassed $17 million in total donations, reflecting support from more than 60,000 donors over five years.The fund honors Allen's late grandmother and supports children receiving treatment at Golisano Children's Hospital. Its impact includes funding critical pediatric equipment, including an ECMO machine and a specialized transport ambulance.The $17 million milestone represents the fund's overall fundraising achievement, rather than Allen's personal donations alone. Contributions from supporters and fundraising initiatives have helped drive that total.How much could Josh Allen's new charity caps raise?At the listed price of $49.99 per cap, purchasing all eight designs would cost $399.92 before taxes and shipping. That figure represents the total retail cost of the collection, not the amount donated to the hospital.The campaign's ultimate financial impact will depend on how many caps are sold and how much of the proceeds are directed to the Patricia Allen Fund. Without a disclosed donation-per-cap figure or sales total, it is not yet possible to calculate the new collection's charitable contribution.Allen's partnership with New Era also extends beyond the retail collection. Game-worn caps are expected to be auctioned after the 2026 season, offering another potential source of fundraising for the cause.For the Bills quarterback, the initiative connects his football visibility with a cause that carries personal significance. For the hospital, it offers another way to engage supporters and raise funds for pediatric care.With the Patricia Allen Fund already surpassing $17 million in total donations and the previous cap auctions generating $140,230, the new collection gives Allen and his supporters another opportunity to build on that success. articles.title: Packers activate Josh Jacobs; running back set to play in first game since domestic violence arrest
articles.summary: Josh Jacobs returns to the Green Bay Packers lineup against the Detroit Lions after six games on the commissioner's exempt list following his arrest.
articles.body: Fresh off the commissioner's exempt list, Josh Jacobs will play in his first game on Sunday since his arrest on charges of domestic violence earlier this year. The Green Bay Packers running back landed on the list following the alleged incident, missing the team's first six games. But the team activated him on Saturday, and he will likely be the team's lead back in their NFC North matchup against the Detroit Lions. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The league continues to investigate Jacobs' situation despite Jacobs' plea of no contest to both misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor criminal damage to property. Jacobs being removed from the list doesn't hinder the investigation, the NFL has noted, but he is allowed back with the Packers. Jacobs was placed on the commissioner’s exempt list Aug. 30, three days after charges were filed against him. His status on the commissioner’s exempt list prevented him from playing or practicing, but he still could prepare himself in other ways. "He could go to meetings," head coach Matt LaFleur said earlier this week. "He could lift with our strength coaches and condition with them. He couldn’t go to any of the team activities – the practices and what not." Green Bay (4-2) has won three straight, but is averaging just 59.8 yards rushing per game – 16.2 fewer than anyone else. The Packers also are last in the league in yards per carry (2.9). MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong Jr. all have been given chances to establish themselves. None have been productive. Jacobs ran for 929 yards and 13 touchdowns while gaining 4 yards per carry last year. That followed a 2024 season in which he rushed for 1,329 yards and 15 touchdowns while making the Pro Bowl. Jacobs spoke with reporters earlier this week, expressing remorse for his actions. TRUMP SAYS NFL 'COULD'VE PROBABLY POSTPONED' PARIS GAME AS FRANCE PROTESTS STRETCH POLICE THIN "Excited to be back with the team, with the guys," he said during his media availability. "I want to say thank you to the organization really for supporting me throughout this whole process and how everything played out. "With that being said, I can't really get into a lot of things, like specifics of things, but obviously I'm remorseful, and sorry for putting this (team) in this situation. "Sometimes, when you go through life, situations occur, and a four-second, three-second decision can alter your life honestly. With that being said, still a human being, man, still trying to learn, still trying to grow from the whole process. Actually learned a lot throughout this whole process, legally and just personally." Jacobs also filed a civil suit last week calling for an injunction and a protective order surrounding evidence, specifically surveillance footage of the incident, which would restrict access to records of the case. articles.body:
With the No. 7 Ole Miss football team taking on the No. 19 Texas Longhorns on Saturday night, it will be another opportunity for quarterback Trinidad Chambliss to show he's one of the better players in his position in the country. As the Ole Miss football quarterback in Chambliss looks to even impress NFL scouts , this former player has given him the label of the best signal-caller in the nation.

If there is a player that could recognize greatness, it is Charles Woodson , who won the Heisman Trophy with the Michigan Wolverines in 1997 and went on to have a Hall of Fame NFL career. Speaking on Big Noon Kickoff on Fox Sports, Woodson would give his prediction for Saturday's contest with the Rebels taking on the Longhorns, saying that Chambliss is the "best quarterback in college football."

Woodson would even give him a nickname, calling him a "magician."

"This team has the best quarterback in college football, in my opinion. I'm going with Ole Miss and Trinidad Chambliss. All this team does is beat top, great teams. Trinidad Chambliss is one of the best in the game. I call him Trinidad the Magician. Nobody moves around the pocket the way he does. Nobody layers throws the way he does," Woodson said.

So far this season for the Ole Miss football program, Chambliss has thrown for 1,676 yards to go along with 14 touchdowns and four interceptions, plus 127 rushing yards and six scores on the ground. At any rate, Chambliss looks to reinforce Woodson's opinion as he looks to lead the Rebels to a 6-1 total record this season after a potential win over Texas on Saturday night.

articles.title: “We can’t go anywhere": Donna Kelce admits struggling with Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s fame
articles.summary: In 2024, Donna Kelce offered a rare glimpse into the personal cost of raising two NFL superstars.
articles.body: In 2024, Donna Kelce offered a rare glimpse into the personal cost of raising two NFL superstars. While Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce built successful careers and became household names, their mother found herself dealing with a level of attention she never expected. The spotlight brought love from fans, but it also took away some of her privacy. In an interview with Glamour for its Women of the Year: The Moms issue, Donna spoke candidly about fame, parenting, and the difficult choices she made during her marriage. Her reflections revealed the sacrifices behind her sons’ success.Donna Kelce reveals the downside of Travis and Jason Kelce’s fameDonna joined Tina Knowles, Maggie Baird, and Mandy Teefey in Glamour’s October 3, 2024, feature celebrating mothers of famous personalities. Although she appreciates the support her sons receive, their celebrity status has changed how she goes about her daily life.“We can’t go anywhere, really. If we want to do something, you have to rent out the restaurant or the movie theater or whatever. I do get to sneak away every once in a while, and we go to places that nobody knows where they are.”The attention can also cross personal boundaries. Donna recalled the discomfort of being approached for photographs in places where privacy should be expected, including bathrooms.She has learned to navigate the attention while continuing to support her sons. However, she also makes an effort to keep them connected to their roots. Donna often reminds Travis and Jason of their childhood, including broken windows and complaints from neighbours about their energetic behaviour.Those memories serve as a reminder that their lives did not begin with NFL success. For Donna, keeping her sons grounded remains important, even as their careers bring them greater recognition.Donna Kelce reflects on divorce and raising her sons aloneBehind the family's public success lies a personal story of difficult decisions. Donna described motherhood as the hardest job she had ever taken on, particularly because she raised Travis and Jason while managing the demands of her banking career.As a commercial banker, she worked hard to demonstrate that women could build careers and remain independent. She wanted her sons to see that strength through her own actions.Her marriage to Ed Kelce also required difficult choices. The couple recognised that their relationship was no longer working, but they chose to remain together until their sons finished college. They wanted to provide Jason and Travis with stability during their formative years.After their sons graduated, Donna and Ed decided to separate. Despite the end of their marriage, they maintained a friendly relationship and continued to support their children together.Their appearances at NFL games reflected that shared commitment. Even after Jason retired from professional football, both parents continued to stand behind Travis as he pursued his career with the Kansas City Chiefs.Donna's story highlights a side of NFL fame that fans rarely see. Her sons may command attention on the field, but the values that shaped their lives began at home, through years of hard work, sacrifice, and a mother's determination to put her children first.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Last month, Tom Brady turned his legendary NFL career into an opportunity to help others, offering two valuable pieces of memorabilia to support a French charity event. The seven-time Super Bowl champion joined the fundraising effort connected to ZEvent, a major charity streaming event on Twitch. His contribution included a signed helmet and football, giving fans a chance to own items linked to one of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history. Beyond their potential auction value, the donation highlighted how Brady’s sporting legacy can bring together football fans and online communities for a cause bigger than the game.Tom Brady donates signed NFL memorabilia to support ZEvent charityBrady's involvement came through ZEvent, a French fundraising event that brings together online creators to raise money for charitable causes. NFL France announced his participation in a post on X, describing his contribution as an 'insane gift' for French streamer Domingo.The former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback also shared a personal message for those taking part in the event. He said, "I hope the signed helmet and ball are going to make someone happy. I hope you guys enjoy your first NFL game in Paris in October," he said. "Maybe we'll get some cards together someday."The donation offers an unusual connection between American football and France's growing online creator community. With the NFL continuing to expand its international reach, Brady's message also acknowledged the excitement surrounding the league's first regular-season game in Paris, scheduled for October 2026.Signed equipment from a player with Brady's record is highly sought after by collectors. While the final amount raised from the items was not disclosed in the report, their potential value could help the event generate meaningful charitable contributions.Tom Brady's memorabilia collection adds value to charity effortsBrady has long shown an interest in sports memorabilia, collecting items that reflect his career and achievements. He has also invested in the trading card business, with ventures linked to the growing market for collectible sports cards.His latest contribution demonstrates another way that memorabilia can serve a purpose beyond private collections. A signed helmet or football can carry personal meaning for fans while also attracting interest from collectors who value rare pieces of NFL history.Brady has supported charitable initiatives over the years, and his participation in ZEvent introduced his name to an audience beyond the traditional American football fan base.The donation also comes amid public discussion surrounding his recent Gucci campaign. However, the charity effort offered a separate focus on his willingness to contribute items from his career to a fundraising cause.For Domingo and the ZEvent community, Brady's involvement added a high-profile NFL name to the event. For fans, it offered a reminder that a sports legend's influence can extend beyond the field, especially when treasured career memorabilia helps support charitable work.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Andy Reid and his wife, Tammy Reid, have built a marriage that has lasted more than four decades, standing together through career changes, family
articles.body: Andy Reid and his wife, Tammy Reid, have built a marriage that has lasted more than four decades, standing together through career changes, family heartbreak and the demands of professional football. However, recent claims suggesting the couple may have separated have raised questions among Kansas City Chiefs fans. The reports have not been confirmed by either Andy or Tammy. Their recent appearance together at a Chiefs game has also drawn attention, offering a different picture from the speculation surrounding their relationship. For now, there is no verified confirmation that the longtime couple is heading for divorce.Andy Reid and Tammy Reid divorce rumours remain unconfirmedA report from USA Tells, attributed to journalist Fiona Ainsworth, claimed Tammy had decided to go her separate way after years of growing differences. It cited Andy's demanding football schedule, differing retirement priorities and alleged emotional distance as possible reasons.However, the claims remain unverified. Neither Andy nor Tammy has publicly confirmed a separation, and their recent appearance at the Chiefs-Raiders game offered no clear evidence of a relationship breakdown.A video shared by insider Farzin Vousoughian showed Andy walking towards the tunnel, where Tammy was waiting for him. The couple shared a kiss before walking away together, a moment that drew attention amid the divorce speculation.Their public appearance does not establish the private details of their marriage, but it is important to distinguish unconfirmed reports from verified facts.Andy and Tammy first met while he played football at Brigham Young University. Their relationship developed into a romance, and they married in 1981. Together, they raised five children, three sons and two daughters. Their family also endured the devastating loss of their son Garrett in 2012.Andy Reid's wife Tammy has supported his NFL career for decadesTammy has remained a steady presence throughout Andy's coaching journey, from his early days at BYU to his time with the Philadelphia Eagles and his successful tenure with the Kansas City Chiefs. Andy has often spoken warmly about their relationship.After winning Super Bowl LIV, he said, “I’ve been … with her for about 40 years now,” Andy said after winning Super Bowl LIV. “Every day is a special day, I’m telling ya. I call her my girlfriend for that reason. You never lose interest if you do that, right, you guys out there? Call them your girlfriend and you always do special things for them.”Tammy has also expressed strong faith in her husband's coaching ability. In a Chiefs profile, she said, “Maybe people don’t know this about me but I’m a very positive person and I have the ultimate trust in Andrew as a coach,” Tammy explained in a Chiefs profile of Andy. “We’ve been through 38 years of coaching and so I never don’t think we’re going to win.”Beyond football, Tammy has supported charitable causes, including Laurel House, a domestic violence organisation she became involved with while living in Philadelphia. She has also participated in community initiatives in Kansas City.For now, claims about an Andy Reid and Tammy Reid divorce remain unconfirmed. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ $325 million KC Current extend historic unbeaten home run to 31 matches
articles.summary: The Kansas City Current have another postseason to prepare for, giving owners Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes another reason to celebrate their
articles.body: The Kansas City Current have another postseason to prepare for, giving owners Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes another reason to celebrate their investment in women’s soccer. The club has secured its third consecutive National Women’s Soccer League playoff berth, overcoming a season of major changes to remain among the league’s contenders. However, qualification is only the first step. With home-field advantage still up for grabs, Kansas City faces an important final stretch that could shape its chances of making a deep postseason run.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ KC Current eye home playoff advantageThe Current officially secured their playoff place after the Portland Thorns defeated the North Carolina Courage 1-0 on Friday night, October 23. Kansas City, Utah Royals and Portland Thorns each have 47 points, placing the three clubs in the playoff picture.For Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes, who are part of the Current’s ownership group, the achievement reflects the club’s continued competitiveness despite a challenging campaign.Kansas City will host the Washington Spirit on Sunday, October 25, in its final home match of the regular season. The match carries extra importance because a victory could strengthen the Current’s chances of earning a top-four seed and hosting a playoff game.The club also hopes to welcome 18,000 supporters for its annual fan appreciation match, potentially setting another attendance record. Strong home support has been a defining feature of Kansas City’s season, with the team remaining unbeaten across 31 consecutive home matches, an NWSL record.Head coach Chris Armas has faced a demanding first season in charge of a women’s team. Roster changes and shifting availability have tested the squad, but the Current have continued to collect important results.KC Current rely on Temwa Chawinga and Croix Bethune before Decision DayKansas City’s home form has helped offset its inconsistent results away from home. The team has recorded a 10-0-4 home record, compared with a 4-1-9 mark on the road.The Current have scored 50 goals this season, including 37 at home. Temwa Chawinga remains a major attacking threat, leading the team with 12 goals despite missing matches through injury and international duty.Croix Bethune has also made a significant impact. Her 10 assists have matched the NWSL single-season record, which she shares with Utah’s Cloé Lacasse.The next challenge will be maintaining that momentum when the regular season concludes. On Decision Day, November 1, Kansas City will face Racing Louisville, currently 15th in the standings. All 16 teams are scheduled to play at 4 p.m. Central Time.The NWSL playoffs begin with the quarterfinals from November 6 to 8. For the Mahomes-owned club, securing a favourable seed could provide a valuable advantage as it pursues another postseason run.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion has become the centre of a growing neighborhood dispute, with concerns about privacy, property boundaries and
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion has become the centre of a growing neighborhood dispute, with concerns about privacy, property boundaries and the look of the lakefront estate complicating his plans. The Kansas City Chiefs star has faced fresh resistance from residents in Bratenahl, where local officials have approved parts of the proposed landscaping but rejected other elements. Despite efforts to address objections, the project remains unfinished, forcing Kelce’s team to revisit its plans as tensions with longtime neighbors continue to simmer.Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million mansion faces another planning hurdleThe dispute surrounding Kelce’s luxury property has taken another turn after a village review board declined to approve trees proposed along the shoreline. Officials also placed conditions on parts of the front landscaping, leaving the project with more work to complete before the estate’s outdoor plans can move forward.Kelce’s property in Bratenahl, near Cleveland, spans approximately 21,000 square feet and includes eight bedrooms, 11 bathrooms, a guest cottage, a swimming pool and a converted ballroom and game room. The scale of the estate has brought added attention to plans for privacy and landscaping in the established lakeside community.The proposed six-foot aluminum fence has also drawn objections. Residents raised concerns about its appearance, its potential effect on wildlife and whether it would provide meaningful protection from unwanted attention. One neighbor warned that deer could become trapped on the fence’s pointed tops.The review process has highlighted the challenge of balancing a high-profile homeowner’s security needs with local rules designed to protect lake views, neighborhood character and property values.Travis Kelce’s landscaping plans spark wider neighborhood concernsSewer infrastructure remains one of the concerns raised by neighboring residents, but it is not the only issue holding up the project.Katherine Bolton, who has lived next door for 35 years, questioned plans to plant around 50 evergreen trees near an old clay sewer line. She said the roots could cause serious damage and cited a potential $75,000 repair bill for lining the pipe.“Planting 50 evergreen trees just ten feet from a 100-year-old clay sewer line is virtually guaranteed to cause severe root intrusion, pipe structural failure, and catastrophic sewage backups,” she said, citing AI-based research.Kelce’s construction team has pushed back by pointing to changes made in response to residents’ complaints. Project representative Jacob Kutz said the owners had already paid $7,500 to repair a damaged section of the sewer line without seeking contributions from the neighbors.The team also moved the fence two feet inside the property boundary, added access gates and paid to trim trees on neighboring land.Those adjustments have not resolved every disagreement. The board has allowed some landscaping work but wants a revised proposal for the shoreline trees.For Kelce, the next step is to return with a plan that addresses the remaining objections while meeting the village’s requirements. Until then, the mansion’s landscaping project remains caught between private property plans and the expectations of the surrounding community.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Raiders mourn Super Bowl champion Pete Banaszak, key figure in iconic 'Holy Roller' play
articles.summary: Pete Banaszak scored twice in the Raiders' Super Bowl XI victory over the Vikings and played a key role in the infamous "Holy Roller" NFL play.
articles.body: Former Oakland Raiders standout Pete Banaszak, a 13-year veteran who helped the franchise win its first Super Bowl, died at 82, the team announced. "The Raiders Family mourns the passing of Pete Banaszak, whose toughness, competitive spirit, and dedication embodied a legendary era of Raiders football and made him a cherished member of the Silver and Black," the team said in a statement released Saturday. The Raiders also remembered the late running back's deep pride in his Polish heritage and extended their condolences to his loved ones. "A Wisconsin native, Banaszak was fiercely proud of his Polish heritage and was inducted into the National Polish-American Sports Hall of Fame in 1990. The deepest condolences of the entire Raider Nation are with Pete's wife Sue, daughters Rebecca and Amy, grandsons Luke, Austin, and Connor, and all of his loved ones." RAIDERS LEGEND GIVES BLESSING TO FIRST OVERALL PICK FERNANDO MENDOZA TO WEAR NO. 15: 'HE'S PERFECT' Banaszak was primarily a reserve during his career, starting just 36 of the 173 NFL games he played. Even so, he made the most of his opportunities and etched his name into Raiders lore during his 13 seasons with the famed Silver and Black. Banaszak made his final appearance with the Raiders in 1978. His best season came in 1975, when he rushed for a league-high 16 touchdowns and a career-best 672 yards in his 10th year with the franchise. Those 16 rushing touchdowns remain a Raiders single-season record. CRAIG MORTON, QUARTERBACK WHO LED THE BRONCOS TO THEIR FIRST SUPER BOWL APPEARANCE, DEAD AT 83 Banaszak crossed the goal line twice in the Raiders’ Super Bowl XI victory over the Minnesota Vikings. The win marked the first time the franchise won the Vince Lombardi Trophy. Banaszak also played a key role in one of the NFL’s most famous plays, the "Holy Roller." In Week 2 of what would be his final season, the Raiders trailed the Chargers 20-14 with seconds remaining when Ken Stabler fumbled while seemingly being sacked. Banaszak recovered and batted the ball forward, giving tight end Dave Casper a chance to make the recovery in the end zone. The extra point secured Oakland’s improbable 21-20 win.
